import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1102

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1102)
-/
open Squarefree Set Order Filter Topology
namespace Erdos1102

/--
Property P : A set $A ⊆ ℕ $ has property P, if for all $n ≥ 1$ the set
$ \{a ∈ A | n + a\text{ is squarefree}\}$ is finite.
-/
def HasPropertyP (A : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n ≥ 1, {a ∈ A | Squarefree (n + a)}.Finite

/--
Property Q : A set $A ⊆ ℕ $ has property Q, if the set
$\{n ∈ ℕ  | ∀ a ∈ A, n > a\text{ implies }n + a\text{ is squarefree}\}$ is infinite.
-/
def HasPropertyQ (A : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  {n : ℕ | ∀ a ∈ A, a < n → Squarefree (n + a)}.Infinite

/--
If `A = {a₁ < a₂ < …}` has property P,
then `A` has natural density `0`.
Equivalently, `(a_j / j) → ∞` as `j → ∞`.
--/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/1e075c4f6e8a907b924647fa88238f978e941742/ErdosProblem1102PropertyP.lean"]
theorem erdos_1102.density_zero_of_P
    (A : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h_inc : StrictMono A)
    (hP : HasPropertyP (range A)) :
    Tendsto (fun j => (A j / j : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Conversely, for any function `f : ℕ → ℕ` that goes to infinity,
there exists a strictly increasing sequence `A = {a₁ < a₂ < …}`
with property P such that `(a_j / j) ≤ f(j)` for all `j`.
--/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/1e075c4f6e8a907b924647fa88238f978e941742/ErdosProblem1102PropertyP.lean"]
theorem erdos_1102.exists_sequence_with_P
    (f : ℕ → ℕ) (h_inf : Tendsto f atTop atTop)
    (h_pos : ∀ n, f n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧
    HasPropertyP (range A) ∧
    ∀ j : ℕ, (A j : ℝ) / j ≤ f j := by
  sorry

/--
Every sequence with property Q has upper density at most `6 / π^2`.
--/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/1e075c4f6e8a907b924647fa88238f978e941742/ErdosProblem1102PropertyQDensity.lean"]
theorem erdos_1102.upper_density_Q
    (A : ℕ → ℕ) (h_inc : StrictMono A)
    (hQ : HasPropertyQ (range A)) :
    limsup (fun j : ℕ  ↦ (j / A j : ℝ)) atTop ≤ 6 / Real.pi^2 := by
  sorry

/--
There exists an infinite sequence $A = {a₁ < a₂ < …} ⊂ \mathsf{SF}$ where
$\mathsf{SF} := \mathbb{N} \setminus \bigcup_{p} p^{2}\mathbb{N}$, i.e. the set of
squarefree numbers. The set `A` has property `Q` and natural density `6 / π^2`.
Equivalently, `(j / a_j) → 6/π^2` as `j → ∞`.
--/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/1e075c4f6e8a907b924647fa88238f978e941742/ErdosProblem1102PropertyQDensity.lean"]
theorem erdos_1102.lower_density_Q_exists :
    ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧
    (∀ j, Squarefree (A j)) ∧
    HasPropertyQ (range A) ∧
    Tendsto (fun j : ℕ  ↦ (j / A j : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (6 / Real.pi^2)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1102

reformulations.difference: The source requires infinitely many positive integers n; Lean permits n = 0 among the witnesses.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Removing the singleton {0} from an infinite set preserves infinitude. Thus the definition is equivalent to requiring infinitely many n satisfying both 0 < n and the same squarefreeness condition. This equivalence was proved for every A in Review1102.hasQ_positive_witness_iff.

reformulations.difference: The source uses positive-indexed, positive-valued sequences. Lean uses A : ℕ → ℕ, includes j = 0 in the bound, and explicitly requires f to be nonzero-valued.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source's natural numbers are positive, so h_pos expresses its codomain convention. Its f can be extended to index 0 with any positive value. Extend a source sequence by A 0 = 0 and A j = a_j for j ≥ 1: strict monotonicity is preserved, adding one element preserves P, and the zeroth inequality is 0 ≤ f 0. Conversely, discard the zeroth entry without reindexing the positive entries; StrictMono gives A j ≥ j ≥ 1, P passes to subsets, and all required bounds remain unchanged. The fixed-f existential equivalence was proved in Review1102.rate_claim_indexing_iff.

reformulations.difference: The source bounds the upper density defined using counting functions; Lean bounds limsup j / A j.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a strictly increasing enumeration, the positive-element count at A j is j or j + 1, depending on whether A 0 = 0. Between consecutive positive sequence elements, the count is constant and its quotient by x decreases. Hence its upper density equals limsup j / A j: the possible difference 1 / A j tends to zero. Finite sets in the source have density zero automatically. Allowing A 0 = 0 is harmless for the universal bound, since removing zero preserves Q and density. Lean checks also established j ≤ A j, the bound 0 ≤ j / A j ≤ 1, and the exact count below A j; thus no real-limsup default case is involved. The full limsup equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses j / A j → 6 / π², whereas the paper explicitly gives the equivalent growth formulation A j / j → π² / 6.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both limits are nonzero, and inversion is continuous there. Taking reciprocals transforms either limit into the other. Review1102.reciprocal_density_form proves this exact equivalence. Starting the enumeration at zero rather than one does not affect the limit; Squarefree (A j) also excludes zero-valued sequence terms.
